title: Physics-driven proper orthogonal decomposition for partial differential equations
author: Pulimeno, Coates-Farley, et al.

steps.title: Method of snapshots for calculations of pod modes
steps.instruction: From Eq. (2), the average of the tensor product can be expressed as follows [19,20]:(4)〈Q(r→,t)⊗Q(r→′,t)〉=1Ns∑j=1NsQ(r→,tj)Q(r→′,tj).

steps.title: Method of snapshots for calculations of pod modes
steps.instruction: Hence, the eigenvalue problem in Eq. (2) can be rewritten as:(5)1Ns∑j=1NSQ(r→,tj)∫Ω′Q(r→′,tj)η(r→′)dΩ′=λη(r→).

steps.title: Method of snapshots for calculations of pod modes
steps.instruction: Now, define the projection of the sampled data onto the POD space as:(6)u(tj)=∫Ω′Q(r→′,tj)η(r→′)dΩ′, and the eigenvalue problem of Eq. (5) then becomes:(7)1Ns∑j=1NSQ(r→,tj)u(tj)=λη(r→).

steps.title: Method of snapshots for calculations of pod modes
steps.instruction: Multiplying both sides of Eq. (7) by Q(r→,ti)and performing integration over the domain Ω, the following equation is derived:(8)1Ns∑j=1Ns[∫ΩQ(r→,ti)Q(r→,tj)dΩ]u(tj)=λ∫ΩQ(r→,ti)η(r→)dΩ.

steps.title: Method of snapshots for calculations of pod modes
steps.instruction: With the matrix element defined as:(9)Aij=1Ns∫ΩQ(r→,ti)Q(r→,tj)dΩ,the eigenvalue problem in the sampling domain can be written as:(10)Au→=λu→.

steps.title: Method of snapshots for calculations of pod modes
steps.instruction: Once the eigenvectors are determined, the POD modes can be obtained via the linear combination of numerical observations:(11)ηi(r→)=1λNs∑j=1NsQ(r→,tj)ui(tj).
